headline: Hidden in the Amazon: Scientists Name a New Frog Species
meta_description: A newly discovered frog species in the western Amazon reveals how much biodiversity remains unknown—and why naming it matters for conservation.
summary_short: Scientists identified Adenomera varcena, a previously unknown frog living in Amazon floodplain forests, using DNA analysis and acoustic recordings.
body:
In the seasonally flooded forests of the western Amazon, researchers have identified a frog species that was hiding in plain sight. Named Adenomera varcena, the newly discovered amphibian was found near the Upper Juruá River region in Acre, Brazil, and formally described in the journal Ichthyology & Herpetology. Although the frog looks nearly identical to its close relatives, scientists distinguished it through DNA analysis, its distinctive mating call, and physical features—including the absence of a dark spot on its forearm. The discovery underscores a scientific challenge known as cryptic diversity: animals that appear almost identical can actually be separate species entirely.

What makes this frog particularly significant is where it lives. Members of the genus Adenomera are typically associated with dryland forests, but Adenomera varcena thrives in varcena—Amazonian floodplain forests that are submerged during certain seasons. This habitat preference suggests the genus is far more ecologically diverse than previously understood. Researchers, including Célio F. B. Haddad from São Paulo State University, also found evidence that numerous other Adenomera lineages remain undescribed, hinting at how much amphibian diversity still awaits formal recognition.

The discovery carries urgent conservation implications. Because seasonal flooding patterns may shift due to climate change, the frog's specific dependence on floodplain ecosystems puts it at potential risk—though scientists do not yet fully understand its ecological requirements. More immediately, formally naming the species ensures it can be included in threatened species lists and environmental protections. As habitats disappear faster than scientists can document them, each species description becomes an act of preservation, ensuring that biodiversity is recognized and protected before it vanishes.
quick_facts: New frog species found in western Acre, Brazil's Upper Juruá River region
Named Adenomera varcena after its floodplain forest habitat
Identified through DNA, acoustic calls, and body morphology comparisons
First Adenomera species known to prefer seasonally flooded forests
Formal naming protects species under conservation and environmental laws
